input_messages.content: Hi there. I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.
I’m not sure about the calls and texts right now, but I just checked my phone and I see a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something important? Am I supposed to turn that off?

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now, at the top of my phone, I see something that says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” Is that normal? I’m still not sure if I can send a picture message yet. What should I do next?

Alright, I went ahead and took out the SIM card and put it back in. Now I see some signal bars at the top, and it says “2G” and “Data Enabled.” Is that good? Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there something else I need to do?

Okay, I changed the network mode like you said, and now it shows “5G” at the top with full bars and “Data Enabled.” Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there anything else I need to check first? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right.

I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. It’s really frustrating—everything looks like it should work, but the message just won’t send. Is there something else I need to do?

I checked my phone’s APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not sure if that’s right or not. Do I still need to reset anything, or are these the correct settings?

I’ve reset the APN settings like you said, but it says the changes will only take effect after I restart my phone. I’m a bit nervous about restarting—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I do this?

Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—everything seems to be set up right, but it just won’t work. Is there anything else we can try?
It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on right now. Should I go ahead and turn that off, or do you want to walk me through it? I’m not always sure where to find these settings.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else I should try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it has permission for SMS and phone, but I don’t see anything about storage. Could that be the problem? If so, how do I give it permission for storage?

Alright, I gave the messaging app permission to access storage like you said. I just tried sending a picture message, and it finally worked! Thank you so much for your help and patience—I really appreciate it.
Thank you so much for your patience and for guiding me through everything. I really appreciate your help. Have a great day! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi there. I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you with your MMS issue.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Thank you for providing your information, John. I have located your account. To help you fix the MMS (picture messaging) issue, I’ll need to guide you through a few quick checks and steps on your phone.

First, can you confirm:
- Are you able to make regular calls and send/receive standard text messages (SMS)?
- Are you currently connected to mobile data (not just Wi-Fi)?

Once you confirm, I’ll walk you through the next troubleshooting steps for MMS.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I’m not sure about the calls and texts right now, but I just checked my phone and I see a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something important? Am I supposed to turn that off?

Yes, the airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless communications—including cellular service, calls, texts, and MMS—are disabled. This is likely the reason you’re unable to send picture messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon to disable it.

Once you’ve turned off Airplane Mode, check if you can send an MMS. Let me know if the issue is resolved or if you need further assistance.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now, at the top of my phone, I see something that says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” Is that normal? I’m still not sure if I can send a picture message yet. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Seeing “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” means your phone is not currently connected to the cellular network or mobile data, which is required for sending MMS.

Let’s troubleshoot further:
1. First, we need to check your SIM card status to ensure it’s properly inserted and active.
2. Then, we’ll make sure your mobile data is enabled.

I’ll start by checking your SIM card status.

Your line ending in 2002 is active, so the SIM card should be working. However, your phone is showing “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” which means it’s not connecting to the network.

Let’s try the following steps:
1. Remove and reinsert your SIM card (this is called “reseating” the SIM). This can help your phone reconnect to the network.
2. After reseating the SIM, check if you see signal bars and if mobile data is enabled.

Please let me know once you’ve reseated your SIM card, or if you need instructions on how to do this.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I went ahead and took out the SIM card and put it back in. Now I see some signal bars at the top, and it says “2G” and “Data Enabled.” Is that good? Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there something else I need to do?

That’s great progress! You now have signal and mobile data enabled. However, since your phone is connected to “2G,” MMS may not work reliably because 2G networks are generally too slow for picture messages.

Let’s improve your connection by switching your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, which are better for MMS and data. Please change your network mode to “4G/5G Preferred” in your phone’s settings.

Once you’ve done that, check if your phone shows “4G” or “5G” at the top. Then, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works or if you need further help.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I changed the network mode like you said, and now it shows “5G” at the top with full bars and “Data Enabled.” Should I try sending a picture message now, or is there anything else I need to check first? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right.

You’ve done everything correctly so far! With “5G” and “Data Enabled” showing at the top, your phone is now in the best state for sending MMS (picture messages).

Please try sending a picture message now. If it goes through, your issue should be resolved. If you still have trouble, let me know, and we can check a few more settings to make sure everything is working as it should.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. It’s really frustrating—everything looks like it should work, but the message just won’t send. Is there something else I need to do?

Thank you for letting me know. Since you have a strong 5G signal and data enabled, the next most common cause for MMS issues is incorrect APN (Access Point Name) settings, which control how your phone connects to our network for data and MMS.

Let’s check your APN settings:
1. Please check your phone’s APN settings and look for the “MMSC URL” or “MMS” section.
2. If you see anything missing or incorrect, you’ll need to reset your APN settings to default.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to check and reset your APN settings, or do you already know how to do this?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my phone’s APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not sure if that’s right or not. Do I still need to reset anything, or are these the correct settings?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. The APN name “internet” and the MMSC URL “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc” look correct for most carriers, but sometimes resetting the APN settings can resolve hidden configuration issues.

Let’s try resetting your APN settings to default:
1. Go to your phone’s APN settings menu.
2. Select the option to “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.”
3. After resetting, please restart (reboot) your phone to apply the changes.

Once your phone restarts, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you still have trouble.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I’ve reset the APN settings like you said, but it says the changes will only take effect after I restart my phone. I’m a bit nervous about restarting—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I do this?

Restarting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or important data. It simply refreshes your phone’s system and applies the new network settings.

Please go ahead and restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try sending a picture message again. If you still have trouble after restarting, let me know and we’ll continue troubleshooting.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—everything seems to be set up right, but it just won’t work. Is there anything else we can try?

Thank you for your patience. Since you’ve reset your APN settings, restarted your phone, and have a strong 5G signal with data enabled, let’s check a few more things that can affect MMS:

1. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your phone? Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS. If it’s on, try turning it off and then send a picture message again.
2. Does your messaging app have permission to access storage and SMS? The app needs these permissions to send and receive MMS.

Could you please check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled and let me know? If you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through the steps.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on right now. Should I go ahead and turn that off, or do you want to walk me through it? I’m not always sure where to find these settings.

Yes, please turn off Wi-Fi Calling, as it can sometimes interfere with sending MMS. Here’s how you can usually do it:

1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Look for “Connections” or “Network & Internet.”
3. Tap on “Wi-Fi Calling.”
4. Toggle the switch to turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF.

Once you’ve turned off Wi-Fi Calling, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you need more help finding the setting.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else I should try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.

Thank you for sticking with the troubleshooting so far. I understand this can be frustrating. There’s one more important thing to check: your messaging app’s permissions.

Your messaging app needs permission to access storage (for photos) and SMS (for sending messages). If these permissions aren’t granted, MMS won’t work.

Could you please check your messaging app’s permissions and make sure both “Storage” and “SMS” are allowed? If you’re not sure how to do this, I can guide you through the steps. Let me know if you need instructions.

App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, phone.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it has permission for SMS and phone, but I don’t see anything about storage. Could that be the problem? If so, how do I give it permission for storage?

Yes, not having storage permission could definitely prevent your messaging app from sending picture messages. To fix this, you’ll need to grant storage permission to your messaging app.

Here’s how you can do it on most Android phones:
1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and select your messaging app from the list.
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Look for “Storage” and set it to “Allow.”

Once you’ve granted storage permission, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you need more help!

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.

Alright, I gave the messaging app permission to access storage like you said. I just tried sending a picture message, and it finally worked! Thank you so much for your help and patience—I really appreciate it.

I’m so glad to hear that your picture messages are working now! You did a great job following all the steps. If you have any more questions or need help with anything else in the future, feel free to reach out. Have a wonderful day!
